messages:
sam r: spotted weird bias where console p50 < metrics-api p50 for /v1/embeddings. p95/p99 look aligned. anyone seen p50 inversion before?
amira: interesting. p50 inversion usually means some lightweight client-side aggregation or dedupe at ingestion changing distribution. can you share a quick sample?
sam r: pasted a 5m export: console p50=18ms, metrics-api event_time p50=42ms. p95 both ~220ms. counts match ~420k.
tj: do we aggregate per-client then rollup? per-client bucketing can compress mids and shift median.
claire: also check proxy dedup. our gateway sometimes emits both request_start and request_end samples and an edge proxy can collapse them into a single sample on ingestion. that will skew lower quantiles.
sam r: here's the diagnostic query I used:
```
GET /internal/metrics/query
{
  "metric": "request_latency_ms",
  "filter": {"endpoint": "/v1/embeddings"},
  "group_by": ["sample_origin", "client_id"],
  "window": {"type": "event_time", "start": "-5m", "end": "now"},
  "aggs": ["p50", "p95" ,"count"]
}
```
claire: sample_origin is critical: possible values: client, gateway, proxy, batcher. console historically hides origin so top-level numbers are opaque. product keeps asking for simpler explanations for "median mismatch" tickets.
amira: proposal: add a percentile-provenance legend in the console showing proportions by sample_origin and show median computed both on raw-event and on per-client pre-aggregated view.
tj: backend implications: computing both raw-event quantiles and pre-agg quantiles doubles some compute. but we can keep raw-event event_time rollups and only compute pre-agg on demand for selected endpoints.
console-bot: UX mock: hover on p50 -> small panel: provenance pie (client 72%, gateway 20%, proxy 8%) + small link "why medians differ" -> expands to per-origin p50/p95 and sample counts.
sam r: in my export: client p50=22ms (n=305k), gateway p50=15ms (n=95k), proxy p50=48ms (n=20k). overall p50 ends up closer to gateway due to ingestion dedupe.
claire: edge case: batcher emits aggregated sample representing many requests as single sample with aggregated latency. if we treat aggregated sample as one point, quantiles are wrong. we must weight by sample_count when aggregating.
amira: good call. we should ensure rollups record sample_count metadata and make percentiles computed on weighted samples where applicable. that will fix batcher artifacts.
tj: ops suggestion: add a small telemetry detect rule that flags endpoints where event_time p50 > ingestion p50 by >20% and sample_origin mix suggests dedupe or batching. alerts go to telemetry-sleuth channel not paged unless SLO violated.
sre-bot: opened telemetry ticket: INFR-3290 - "percentile provenance + weighted rollups" assigned to amira. includes sample dump and UX mock.
claire: dev note: protobuf ingestion schema already has sample_count but we strip it for low-cardinality rollups; need to keep it. likely small storage bump.
amira: rough impact: keep sample_count in top-level rollups + add optional weighted-percentile comp path. storage +8%, cpu +12% for rollups but we can gate by tenant and endpoint whitelist.
sam r: product ask: also show "reason" label for chart anomalies. e.g. "median inversion due to client-side aggregation" so customer-facing alerts are actionable.
console-bot: scheduled follow-up sync: telemetry design review tomorrow 4pm PT. invite sent. :calendar:
tj: thanks everyone. if we can get provenance pie + weighted percentile quickfix in the next sprint, it should cut down on support tickets. :thumbsup:
